solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Judges inquire before one's second act of treachery

parts.note: Jud is the standard abbreviation for the Book of Judges in the Bible
to inquire is to ask
one is I, so one's is I'S

explanation.surface: A court asks questions before someone commits a second act of betrayal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judges' looks like people in court but is the biblical book, abbreviated JUD.
explanation.definitionFit: The kiss Judas gave Jesus in Gethsemane to betray him became the byword for a treacherous gesture.

clue.text: First person in France included extraterrestrial chart for high flier

indicators.note: the French pronoun takes the following pieces inside it

parts.note: the French for 'I' is je
a chart is a plan

explanation.surface: A Frenchman draws an alien's map for someone going up high.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet aircraft flies at great altitude, so it is literally something that flies high.

clue.text: I am up in easily managed abode

indicators.note: the reversed letters go inside the word for easily managed

parts.note: a docile animal or person is easily managed

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm

explanation.surface: Someone says they are awake and up in a manageable home.
explanation.definitionFit: A domicile is a formal word for one's home or place of residence, synonymous with abode.

clue.text: Old penniless top dogs arranging economic policy

indicators.note: arranging the remaining letters puts them in a new order
d stood for the old British penny, so penniless means losing that letter

explanation.surface: Bankrupt former bigwigs are drawing up an economic policy.
explanation.walkthrough: D was the abbreviation for a penny in pre-1971 British money; dropping it from TOPDOGS leaves TOPOGS, rearranged by 'arranging'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stop-go was the British name for alternating restraint and expansion in government economic management.

clue.text: At home yet not at home to some extent

parts.note: someone at home is said to be in
someone not at home is away

explanation.surface: A paradox: somebody is both home and not home, partly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'in a way' means partly or in some respects, matching to some extent.

clue.text: Star in the roof?

parts.note: a star is a light in the sky, and a roof window lets the sky's light in

explanation.surface: An actor appears up on the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A window set into a roof is named for admitting daylight, so the clue plays on lights in the sky.

clue.text: Common sense, very very little for instance outside

indicators.note: the word for 'for instance' goes around the shortened intensifiers

parts.note: say is used to mean for instance
each very shortened to its abbreviation V gives two Vs

explanation.surface: Someone notes there is very, very little common sense around, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: Savvy is informal for shrewd practical know-how, which is what common sense amounts to.

clue.text: Personality, a medium in London area has the very thing

parts.note: one's self is one's personality

indicators.note: the article and the size letter sit within the postal district

parts.note: SE is the south-east London postal district
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: A personality and a psychic in a London district have exactly the thing wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medium' suggests a psychic but is just M, as on a clothes label; in 'the very thing', very can be swapped for selfsame.
explanation.definitionFit: Selfsame means identical or exactly the same, the sense very has in 'the very place'.

clue.text: There's absolutely nothing in it

parts.note: sounds like a dismissal of a rumour, but literally describes a space emptied even of air

explanation.surface: Someone denies there is any truth in a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacuum is a space entirely empty of matter, so literally nothing is inside it.

clue.text: Rodney floundering in the distance

indicators.note: floundering means struggling clumsily, so the letters of the name are thrown about

explanation.surface: A man called Rodney is struggling somewhere far off.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonder is an old word meaning over there, at some distance away.

clue.text: Thomas taking said hat from draw!

parts.note: Tom is short for Thomas

indicators.note: said tells us the hat's name is to be heard, not written

parts.note: a bowler is a hard round hat

explanation.surface: Thomas pulls a name out of a hat for a prize draw.
explanation.walkthrough: BOWLER spoken in a non-rhotic accent sounds like BOLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a lottery or raffle in which tickets are drawn from a revolving drum.

clue.text: Fully equipped spring discovered

parts.note: a well is a spring of water
found means discovered

explanation.surface: A spring of water has been found.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-found describes a ship or place furnished with everything needed, i.e. fully provided.

clue.text: Ex-allowance

parts.note: reads as a former allowance but means money paid to an ex-spouse

explanation.definitionFit: After divorce a court may order maintenance payments to one's former partner.

clue.text: Rules for language school

definitions.meaning: the structural rules governing how words combine
a ... school, a selective British secondary school

explanation.definitionFit: Grammar is the system of rules of a language and short for a grammar school, a selective British state secondary.

clue.text: Most important building to see in Devon

definitions.text: Most important building to see in Devon

parts.words: Most important building to see in Devon
parts.note: reads as a tourist sight, but a see is a bishop's diocese, whose chief church is its cathedral

explanation.surface: A guide picks the top attraction in the county of Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England; its county town's cathedral is the seat of the bishop of that see.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathedral is the principal church of a diocese, its see, and Devon's diocese has its cathedral in the city of Exeter.

clue.text: Sameness of nearly everybody in union

indicators.note: the shortened word sits inside the union's name

parts.note: Equity is the British actors' trade union

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: everybody is all

explanation.surface: Almost all members of a union are treated alike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' suggests marriage or a trade union generally; here it is the British actors' union specifically, a frequent crossword name.
explanation.definitionFit: Equality is the state of being equal, which is a kind of sameness.

clue.text: Crack made by vicar accepting a vessel in church

indicators.note: the vicar and the ship sit inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
Rev, short for Reverend, is a vicar's title
SS, steamship, is a vessel

explanation.surface: A vicar takes in a vessel in church and something cracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' simply has REV followed by A and SS.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevasse is a deep crack or fissure in a glacier.

clue.text: Cecilia's former country in Africa?

parts.note: reads as a woman named Cecilia's homeland, but splits as Cecil plus -ia, the country named after Cecil Rhodes

explanation.surface: Someone asks which African country a woman named Cecilia once lived in.
explanation.definitionFit: The former African territory, now Zimbabwe and Zambia, was named after the colonialist Cecil Rhodes.

clue.text: Spectator found lone rook circling

indicators.note: circling birds wheel about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher found a single rook flying in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: A looker-on is someone who watches without taking part, like a spectator.

clue.text: Lot giving support to melody

parts.note: to be for something is to support it
a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: A large crowd backs a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot is one's destiny or fortune in life.

clue.text: Hardly cold

parts.note: reads as barely chilly, but means cold enough to have become hard

explanation.definitionFit: Something frozen has been chilled until it is solid and hard.

clue.text: Scheme for obtaining money dishonestly causes uproar

explanation.surface: A swindle stirs up a public outcry.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is both a dishonest money-making scheme and a loud commotion or din.

clue.text: Instrument used by one getting 200 during game

indicators.note: the number letters come in the middle of the game

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
I is the Roman numeral for one
CC is the Roman numeral for 200

explanation.surface: A musician plays during a match in which someone scores 200.
explanation.definitionFit: The piccolo is a small high-pitched flute, an instrument of the orchestra.

clue.text: Peter's prepared to decide beforehand

indicators.note: preparing the letters puts them into a new arrangement

parts.note: the name with its s used as a letter

explanation.surface: Peter is ready to make up his mind in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: To preset is to set or fix something in advance, deciding it ahead of time.

clue.text: Mad rush that starts after finishing one's education

definitions.text: that starts after finishing one's education

explanation.surface: Graduates rush madly into work after leaving college.
explanation.definitionFit: Career means both a headlong rush and one's working life begun after education.

clue.text: Waver coming from local site

indicators.note: the answer comes out of these letters once they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Uncertainty arises from a nearby site.
explanation.definitionFit: To oscillate is to swing back and forth, hence to waver or vacillate.

clue.text: Nothing taken from extraordinary response from poet

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of its usual order
the zero letter is removed from the word that follows

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A poet gives an extraordinary reply with nothing to it.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing O from RESPONSE leaves RESPNSE, which 'extraordinary' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan poet who wrote The Faerie Queene.

clue.text: Mentally unhinged like Hazel?

definitions.meaning: the hazel tree bears nuts, so it is full of them

explanation.definitionFit: Nutty means crazy, and also tasting of or full of nuts like a hazel tree.

clue.text: Consider what hostess should do

definitions.meaning: to think about or contemplate an idea
a hostess receives and amuses guests

explanation.definitionFit: To entertain is both to consider an idea and to receive and amuse guests as a hostess.
